summary.text: A 65-year-old woman with a history of triple positive breast cancer treated by left radical mastectomy, chemotherapy and hormone therapy, and a prior bilateral hystero-salpingo-oophorectomy, was found about 2 months earlier to have axillary and forearm masses. Imaging and PET showed liver, abdominal, chest and two brain metastases, and the excised node showed metastatic breast cancer, so salvage chemotherapy with paclitaxel, gemcitabine, trastuzumab and pertuzumab was started.

Right leg swelling developed one day after chemotherapy doses, and Doppler ultrasound showed an acute extensive superficial femoral vein thrombus. She was admitted, started on LMWH, had mild pancytopenia with platelets of 60 000, and was discharged two days later. Shortly afterwards she returned with abrupt severe shortness of breath, hypotension of 70 mm Hg, heart rate 155, oxygen saturation 70%, a right ventricular heave and right bundle branch block.

Echocardiography showed severe right ventricular dilation with preserved ejection fraction, and CT angiography confirmed large bilateral pulmonary thromboemboli with right ventricular strain. Thrombolysis was contraindicated by brain metastases and thrombocytopenia, but she was declared inoperable and catheter embolectomy was unavailable, so alteplase 100 mg was infused over 2 hours despite the contraindications.

About an hour after thrombolysis norepinephrine was stopped, blood pressure returned to 110/70 mm Hg and oxygen saturation was 90%. Half-dose heparin was stopped at 30 hours for a platelet drop to 23 000 and platelets were transfused, then heparin was resumed and changed to enoxaparin. She improved, was discharged after 5 days with LMWH, and survived with mild right ventricular dysfunction on the last echocardiogram.
